description: issue #688 (terminal slice): the OTHER `ol-type` branch of `every`'s tick count (spec/interaction-events.md:169 lists `ol-type`, `ol-range`; the profile error table at :350 gives `ol-type` for `an argument has the wrong type`). The sibling `every-non-whole-type-error` covers a value that IS a number but is not whole (`2.5`); this one covers a value that is not a number at all -- the word `"soon"` -- which reaches a different arm of the same check (`params.actual` is `word`, not `number`). Note this is NOT a blanket rejection of words: `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so `every "2"` is legal (pinned by the sibling `every-numeric-word-accepted`); what this pins is the complement, a word that does not parse as a number. Without it, an implementation that validated only wholeness on values already known to be numbers, and mishandled a non-number by some other code or by coercing it, would still pass the corpus. As with every other failed `every` validation, the registration `instruction` is emitted first and the check fails BEFORE the handler is registered, so no `primitive` event is emitted and nothing is registered; the span covers just the offending argument. NOTE: `params.expected` reads `whole number` here while `wait`'s twin (`wait/wait-non-number-type-error`) reads `number` for the identical non-number case -- an observable wording asymmetry between the two primitives' checks, recorded as emitted rather than normalized, since `spec/interaction-events.md` fixes only the `ol-type` CODE for both.

diagnostics.message: every needs a whole number, but got a word.
